findings.failure_path: A pull request can replace the ledger-binding command with a no-op while preserving the job and step names; a required check keyed to that job can then pass without executing the gate. The diff itself supplies no candidate-independent workflow/ruleset control that prevents this.
findings.smallest_fix: Run this check from a protected required workflow whose definition is loaded from a trusted ref or organization ruleset, and provide the corresponding required-check configuration as release evidence.

findings.failure_path: For the one-shot succession challenge, chain_position is 1, so expected_remaining becomes 1 and autonomous_review_allowed must be true. Automation is therefore told another autonomous round is available even though review_gate.py rejects every continuation of that receipt.
findings.smallest_fix: Define succession receipts as terminal in the emitted and validated state: remaining 0, autonomous_review_allowed false, and terminal next-action/human-decision fields; add assertions on the raw succession receipt.

findings.failure_path: Only an empty base reaches the unevaluated branch. A stale, deleted, or mistyped base reaches git diff, raises SystemExit from changed_skill_paths, and reports review_ledger_binding_error rather than the required unevaluated result.
findings.smallest_fix: Resolve the base explicitly before diffing; classify any unresolved revision as review_ledger_binding_unevaluated with the fail-closed exit status, and add a bogus-ref regression case.

findings.failure_path: The real-checkout test verifies only that --print-candidate returns a hash. It does not compare the working tree before and after, so removal of dont_write_bytecode or packet cleanup—and the resulting untracked files under the hashed paths—would not fail this claimed acceptance proof.
findings.smallest_fix: Capture git status including untracked files before and after --print-candidate and assert byte-for-byte equality, with a mutation case that enables the known __pycache__ side effect.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: Succession phase binding is implemented, but the succession receipt still advertises one autonomous round remaining, contradicting its enforced one-shot terminal state.
The merge-side enforcement remains editable by the candidate: a PR can retain the required job name while replacing this step, so the supplied diff cannot establish an enforced merge boundary.
A missing base is classified as unevaluated, but a supplied yet unresolvable base escapes as a generic error, leaving the stated base-resolution behavior incomplete.
The tests exercise candidate matching and succession rejection, but they codify the incorrect succession budget fields and never assert that candidate computation leaves the working tree unchanged.
Historical receipt fields remain structurally compatible, but consumers relying on autonomous_reviews_remaining or autonomous_review_allowed receive misleading succession state.
The scripts are locally reversible and require no data migration, but no candidate-independent workflow or ruleset evidence is supplied to make the new merge gate rollout enforceable.
Candidate mismatch diagnostics are precise; invalid-base classification and the contradictory succession budget indicators would misdirect operators and automation.
The controller blocks chained succession, but the higher-risk merge boundary is not contained because its workflow invocation is modified by the same candidate it is meant to police.
